Deep Rock Galactic ADHD edition: Welcome to the Dopamine Mines

Imagine DRG, but instead of unlocking perks for your character hour by hour by completing missions, you go through the whole progression *within* each mission.

(However, there is still meta progression between runs as well).

It's a game loop inside a game loop. Every 3 minutes you unlock some upgrade, and they can be quite powerful. The best part is, you can mine green ore (Expenite) and directly turn it into weapon upgrades mid run. It's like the joy of finding Nitra or Morkite, distilled into pure dopamine.

The classes are not as hardcoded as in DRG. You go into a mission with a class, which gives you certain special abilities. But all the weapons, grenades, turrets and traversal tools are picked up during the run. There is randomisation here, so you may be forced to pick a weapon you wouldn't have used otherwise.

Game is great solo, the Combat Drone "Cooper" is very strong and each time you level up, you can also pick an upgrade for him.

One fair warning: You need around a one hour commitment for a mission. You need to clear four dungeon floors in a row, and while it would be possible to blast through each one in a few minutes, you are often spending some time navigating, exploring side areas for additional chests and minerals so you can get more upgrades, and are busy choosing between them. At first I was put off by the commitment, but I ended up having so much fun that I am not bothered by it anymore. After all I think certain length is required in order to really become invested into a build.

I also have two nitpicks: The audio seems more horror-themed than it should be (weird screams etc in pause screens). And overall there is less humor than in the original.

I think this game will not replace the original DRG, they both cater to different minds (or moods). Slow steady progression and predictable builds, vs more chaotic and quick progression in a loop.

i loved Deep Rock Galactic but rogue core is just totally missing the mark for me. It feels like you spend most of your time running to somewhere and selecting lame upgrades. There is not nearly enough mining and bugs. I'm very disappointed. I just want DRG 2.

The idea that comparing this game to DRG is the source of discontent is a cop out. Rogue Core is imbalanced and uncertain of what it is trying to do, with some very artificial means of adding difficulty, such as insane amounts of recoil and bullet spread in its weapons.

Much of the game is half baked, and while recent updates have alleviated some of the stressors, the game has a ways to go before it's a solid recommendation.

The most disappointing aspect is that the game was worked on for many years, albeit I'm sure by a small team, and released at its current price as "1.0" and yet also an early access game? These are seemingly contradicting, and if I didn't have friends who play this game I would have returned it and waited until at least "2.0"

I have faith in Coffee Stain and Ghost Ship, they have done wonderful things with DRG and I will always preach about how they're a great studio that doesn't do games as services, and how their creativity created one of my favorite and most recommendable games of all time, all under 10gb. 

I will patiently wait while they find the game they want to make in this early rendition of what could be another hit.

This game might not be for DRG fans, but is definitely for roguelike fans. I am both myself and I really enjoy the path they took with this one, especially melee combat, that is so much more fleshed out. You will fail a lot of missions, sure, but you still get the proportional rewards, therefore it doesn't affect you as much as it did in DRG.

Also alternate site: jumble is my favourite type of mission, where every upgrade is randomized and runs can therefore turn into a very enjoyable experience (e. g. 40 sentry turrets at last boss).

This is a fun alternative of DRG and I really do enjoy it but there is a huge problem; there's really only one type of mission. The gameplay loop does get kind of repetitive really fast. Unlike in the Original DRG, where the missions are different from each other with the main loop being there, Rogue Core doesn't really have a huge difference between missions. Yes, the mining facilities are different, the bioms are different, there are different enemies, there are secondary objectives each round but the main objective never changes and if for playing long period of time in one sitting, you will get bored quite quick especially if you skip all the side content during the missions. It kind of sucks because I really do like playing this game, I do think the design is good, the gun play is fun and this being a "the deepest facilities are completely down because of creatures from the core of Hoxxes" sound completely in character but the gameplay loop just isn't here. There's not enough varity going around and just feels kind of lacking and I usually get off after one game (if I don't die quickly).
very fun, and there's still much improvement and content to come.
Awesome game, needs polishing and performance improvements
Game still need some work. I like it tho.

Rogue Core started off in a bumpy spot with pacing issues and group mechanics at launch which were all rightfully groaned about by the community for some time. That being said it was still plenty of fun and worth the purchase in my opinion even then. Sure there were/are bugs and crashes and matchmaking that sticks you with leaf loving idle brained greenbeards who can wreck some of the first runs you try, but that's just how these types of games operate, especially seeing as this one is still early access. Update 1.1 proved the devs are actively responding to player feedback. They added more upgrades, gave more diversity, removed the drone huddle requirement for upgrades, and even gave the cleaning bot on the Ramrod a nice makeover (the most important thing obviously). Update 1.2 was all about balance and maintaining the purpose of the game. After 1.1 meta-ish builds were much easier to come by, and if you were lucky or had access to google, you could find a way to nuke the boss with ease for which at that point, what is the purpose of even playing? On the subject of reaperworms, they whole point of them is to be your deadline for the elevator. There was a massive surge after 1.1 of players who figured they could just linger around after the reaperworms appeared to get that biobooster a mile away or get that one expenite event done as long as they pop em in the head a few times here or there. There is a method to the madness for Rogue Core. Its not a DRG ripoff where you can try to break the game mechanics being a guns blazing idiot in place of using mods. The bosses shouldn't be nuked and the reaperworms mean its time to go, hence update 1.2. 

If you haven't played the game yet, most of the above commentary is against what others have negatively said. Rogue Core was clearly advertised as a rogue-like with a strict timer which it has very successfully delivered. All the complaints of bugs, lack of content, game mechanics, and boss buffing is akin to whining that an under construction house doesn't have an unapproved indoor pool yet. 

If you want a fast paced rouge-like that's still being aged like wine -> recommend purchase

If you want DRG 2 -> watch the game trailer (or at least some clips) and come back 

If you don't know if you like what you see -> wallet decides if worth the risk. nobody's making you spend a dime

If don't like where the gave is now -> don't buy, just keep tabs on it. It's early access after all

Hey Devs, first of all I love the game so far. I’ve only got a few hours in it but they have been lots of fun, being said here are some of my favourite parts and some parts I want to see be made better.
1) Melee combat,
Melee combat feels nearly impossible. I built a run with slicer where I ran only melee boosting upgrades and the drills. I always felt like I couldn’t do enough damage before I got hit down. The main way I would fix this is to have some melee primary weapons that might now do as much damage to start but could be upgraded like any gun, the pickaxe works as a start but falls behind in the later levels. I love melee combat in games like helldivers and would love to see a better system for this game.

Later note:
I was wrong, melee combat works really well with the right upgrades and if you don't run it as a primary thing. However a no cooldown sword would be very fun.
2) Charge weapons,
Charge weapons feel very underpowered. I tried both the trident and the M1000 classic. Both felt strong while I was shooting but they felt very underpowered compared to weapons with constant uptime, I admit that I don’t have a lot of experience yet and these weapons may become easier to use once I learn more. However, as a beginner I felt like I didn’t have time to react to attacks because I needed to charge for a half second first, with any other weapon I could just shoot a quick burst and carry on but with these weapons I just felt helpless. The way I would want to see this be fixed is to add a held charge like the Minecraft crossbow to avoid sneak attacks.

Later note:
I was wrong a bit, charge weapons aren't as bad as I thought but still don't feel great.
3) my final request,
Please add some healing weapons or a class that heals armour. I love playing support in most shooter games and would love to do the same here, armour feels like a luxury. I often find myself using resupplies just for the armour, but I think a class that does passive slow recovery would be great. I’ve been playing lots of Gaurdian and really enjoying his armour regeneration ability, but I wish it there would be a way to do more. Maybe something similar to ultron’s drones in marvel rivals. That you could switch between your teammates based on who is on the lowest health, or who is gonna pick a fight but still lets you shoot. This would even work as a temporary ability if it had a cooldown. Just having something to give you a better regeneration rather than stealing all the ammo from my team. 

Thank you so much devs for working on making this game the best it can be, I hope that you find this review of any use. Have a great day :)
